newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- Front-page editorial issues stern warning to banks on need to halt speculation in the stock market.
- Central bank holds financial sector meeting in Changsha, Hunan, urging bank officials to curb financial risk.
- Governor of People's Bank Dai Xianglong leaves Beijing for meeting of Bank for International Settlements in Basel, Switzerland.
- Central bank issues renewed notice to creditors of the failed China Agribusiness Trust and investment Co, asking them to register claims with liquidators.
- Administration of State Assets says foreign companies appraising assets in China must obtain temporary licenses.
- China to conduct review of its statistical gathering in bid to clamp down on unreliable and sometimes fraudulent data.
- Premier Li Peng meets Italian counterpart Romano Prodi, hails rising economic cooperation between two countries.
- Sino-U.S. venture formed to produce harvesters in China's northeastern city of Harbin with a total investment of $29.9 million.
- The Ministry of Internal Trade and other ministries set up National Regulation Centre for Commodities Storage in Beijing.
- Zhengzhou commodities futures exchanges moves into new headquarters.
